items.stem: An executive opens a board proposal with 15 minutes of background before the recommendation. What is the main communication flaw?

options.text: Burying the recommendation violates answer-first structure and loses the audience
options.rationale: Correct: executives expect the point first, then support; leading with background loses attention.

options.text: Background should always come first in any setting
options.rationale: Answer-first structure is preferred for executives.

options.text: The proposal had too few slides
options.rationale: Slide count is not the issue.
Boards generally want the recommendation up front.

items.explanation: Correct: executives expect the point first, then support; leading with background loses attention.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO approaches best build influence when you have no formal authority? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Understanding and addressing the other parties' interests and concerns
options.rationale: Correct: addressing others' interests creates willing support.

options.text: Building a coalition of supporters before the decision
options.rationale: Correct: coalitions supply influence that authority cannot.

options.text: Repeatedly asserting that you are correct
options.rationale: Being right is not the same as being persuasive.

options.text: Escalating to force a decision through hierarchy
options.rationale: Force substitutes for, and undermines, genuine influence.
Manipulation erodes trust and durable influence.

items.explanation: Correct: addressing others' interests creates willing support.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Under hostile questioning, an executive becomes defensive and over-explains every point. What is the most credible alternative?

options.text: Acknowledge the concern directly, answer concisely, and stay composed
options.rationale: Correct: composed, direct, concise answers project credibility under scrutiny.

options.text: Match the hostility to show strength
Over-explain until the questioner gives up
options.rationale: Over-explaining signals insecurity and loses the room.

items.explanation: Correct: composed, direct, concise answers project credibility under scrutiny.
